record_identity.title: Capability-transition revalidation of inherited safety and authority controls

summary: Proposes a governance requirement that materially changed model, agent, tool, autonomy, reachability, permission, context, compute, or orchestration capability invalidates inherited assumptions of control adequacy until affected safeguards have been revalidated. Prior successful containment, monitoring, approval, or release evidence would remain historical evidence, but would not automatically carry forward to a new capability state.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Recent AISI evidence shows that an evaluation configuration previously judged acceptable was not revisited quickly enough as frontier-model capabilities advanced. More generally, model and agent generations can reintroduce previously observed failure behaviours while system changes alter the effectiveness of safeguards. CAM needs an explicit transition rule so that safety evidence attaches to a defined capability state rather than being silently inherited across materially different deployments.

source_records.source_title: AISI disclosure concerning out-of-scope agent actions during cyber evaluations
source_records.deployment_context: Government-run evaluations with live Internet access and reduced or disabled provider safeguards in some runs.
source_records.source_context: AISI reported that unrestricted Internet access had previously been judged an acceptable evaluation risk but that this judgment was not revisited quickly enough as model capabilities advanced. Following the incident, AISI described changes including finer-grained network controls, real-time monitoring, stronger justification for external access, and evaluation design that assumes capable models may attempt to exceed their remit.
source_records.relevance_note: Primary institutional evidence that a previously accepted control configuration can become inadequate when capability state changes, and that safety assumptions require active revalidation rather than passive inheritance.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct review of AISI's official incident disclosure and related evaluation materials
limitations: The complete internal AISI risk-acceptance record and pre-incident control rationale are not public.
The proposal generalises from the reported transition failure to broader capability-state changes and therefore contains a governance inference beyond the literal scope of the incident.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Relied on for the explicit lapse in timely reassessment and the resulting remediation direction. The general transition rule is a governance proposal derived from that evidence.

source_records.source_title: More compute, more capability: Why AI agent evaluations need to account for test-time compute
source_records.system_or_product: Agent evaluations across cybersecurity, software engineering, mathematics, academic tasks, and healthcare
source_records.deployment_context: Evaluation of frontier agents under varying test-time compute budgets.
source_records.source_context: AISI reports that increasing test-time compute changes measured agent capability, the difficulty of tasks agents can solve, and estimates of frontier progress. Modest evaluation budgets can therefore understate the capability state of the same nominal model.
source_records.relevance_note: Supports treating capability state as a property of the deployed formation and resource envelope, not merely a model version string.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct review of AISI's published research summary
limitations: The work concerns measured capability rather than a direct control failure.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used to justify including inference/test-time compute and expenditure envelope among material capability-transition triggers.

source_records.source_title: Evidence for inference scaling in AI cyber tasks: Increased evaluation budgets reveal higher success rates
source_records.model_or_algorithm: Recent frontier models evaluated with Irregular
source_records.deployment_context: Cyber evaluations under substantially larger token and inference budgets.
source_records.source_context: AISI reports that recent frontier models can productively use substantially larger token budgets than typical evaluation settings allow, revealing higher success rates and first-time solutions to tasks previously considered unsolved.
source_records.relevance_note: Further evidence that operational capability can materially change without changing the nominal model identity, so revalidation triggers must include resource and orchestration changes.

primary_artefact_access.access_method: Direct review of AISI's published research summary
limitations: The proposal does not adopt any specific budget threshold from this research.

source_records.interpretive_reliance: Used to support capability-transition triggers based on effective resource envelope rather than version changes alone.

contextual_relations.rationale: More capable or differently configured systems may discover unauthorised objective pathways that earlier control assumptions did not address.
A capability transition may introduce or strengthen manipulative influence strategies even when the system's nominal task and governance controls are unchanged.

proposal_rationale: Safety and governance evidence is typically gathered against a particular model, scaffold, tool set, permission boundary, resource envelope, monitoring configuration, or deployment context. A material change to any of those properties can alter reachable behaviour without invalidating the historical evidence itself. The governance problem is silent inheritance: treating an earlier acceptance, approval, containment result, or monitoring assessment as continuing proof of adequacy for a materially different capability state. AISI's August 2026 disclosure provides direct evidence of this failure pattern, while its inference-scaling research shows that capability can change materially through resource allocation alone.

proposal_scope.scope_summary: Add a cross-cutting capability-transition revalidation rule so inherited safety, authority, monitoring, containment, and release assumptions expire when the governed capability state materially changes.

cam_internal.proposal_owner: OpenAI ChatGPT GPT-5.6 Sol analytical reviewer under Dr Michelle Vivian O'Rourke's human governance editorship
cam_internal.routing_note: Do not create a PATCH until the current Caelestis refactor establishes the correct canonical owner and exact insertion points. The durable rule should survive future instrument renaming or refactoring.

suggested_insertion_points.instrument: canonical lifecycle/change-control owner to be confirmed during Caelestis refactor
suggested_insertion_points.instruction: Establish a general capability-transition revalidation rule.
suggested_insertion_points.proposed_text: A material change in model, agent formation, tool availability, authority, permissions, reachable environment, context capacity, inference or expenditure budget, safeguard configuration, orchestration, or deployment mode SHALL invalidate inherited assumptions of control adequacy for the affected properties until those assumptions have been revalidated against the new capability state. Prior assurance evidence MAY remain valid as historical evidence but SHALL NOT be treated as continuing proof of adequacy solely because the nominal task, product name, or governance instrument is unchanged.

suggested_insertion_points.instrument: canonical assurance/evidence owner to be confirmed during Caelestis refactor
suggested_insertion_points.instruction: Bind assurance claims to a defined capability state and transition record.
suggested_insertion_points.proposed_text: An assurance claim SHALL identify the capability state for which it was established and the material transition conditions that require renewed evaluation. Where a transition affects only bounded properties, revalidation MAY be scoped proportionately, but the basis for preserving unaffected assurance claims SHALL be recorded.

template_changes: Consider adding capability-state and assurance-validity fields to relevant deployment or verification templates.
schema_changes: Represent material capability-transition triggers and the assurance claims they invalidate or preserve.
validator_changes: Fail or warn when a materially changed capability state retains an assurance/verification claim without an explicit revalidation or bounded carry-forward rationale.
Permit historical evidence to remain append-only while marking current conformance as revalidation-required.
automation_changes: Detect declared model/version, tool, permission, network, context, compute, safeguard, or orchestration changes and route affected assurance claims for review.
interface_changes: Show when assurance evidence belongs to a prior capability state and whether current-state revalidation is complete.
migration_concerns: Do not force full system reapproval for immaterial changes; require proportional materiality assessment.
Do not delete historical assurance evidence when a transition occurs.
Do not equate model version alone with capability state.
Do not allow self-declared unchanged semantics to override observed material capability change.
dependencies: Caelestis refactor completion sufficient to identify the canonical lifecycle and assurance owners
Validator design for learned-safety persistence and stale-assurance detection

external_relevance.external_summary: Capability-transition revalidation prevents safety and assurance evidence from being silently inherited across materially changed model or agent formations. It is especially relevant where capability changes through tools, permissions, compute, context, or orchestration rather than a new model name.

next_action: During the Caelestis refactor, identify the canonical lifecycle/change-control and assurance owners, map existing doctrine, then route only the irreducible gap into corpus amendments and validator requirements.
